## Season so far

Swift has been a volume back who scores a lot. He has 138.7 half-PPR points in 8 games (17.3 per game) and a career-high 10 rushing TDs. Week 1 against CAR gave him 31.9 points (124 yards, 3 TDs) and is the outlier. He then ran Weeks 2–4 at 10.4, 9.8 and 6.4 points, and his snap share fell to 35% in Week 4. Since Week 5 his role has grown. He had 58%, 58%, 86% and 77% of snaps, then 27 carries and 3 TDs against SEA on Monday night. That game was 26.9 points on 69 yards at 2.6 per carry, so the score came from touchdowns and not from the run game.

## Usage and efficiency

Usage is strong and the efficiency is poor. Over the last 4 games:

- **Snaps:** 70%, up from 64% for the season.
- **Opportunity share:** 35%, up from 32%.
- **Carries:** 74 for 234 yards, which is 3.2 per carry (3.8 on the season).
- **Red zone:** 17 carries (36 on the season).
- **Goal line:** 11 carries (19 on the season).
- **Points:** 20.0 per game, up from 17.3.

Target share is only 11% for the season and 12% over the last 4. He has 24 catches for 162 yards at 5.6 yards per target and no receiving TDs. The receiving work is a small part of his scoring.

The TDs are not a fluke. He has 10 against an expected 10.3 from where his touches came, so the scoring matches his usage. Goal-line work is the base of his value: 19 goal-line carries and none for Roschon Johnson in his place (Johnson has 4 red zone and 4 goal-line carries over the last 4). The risk is that the yardage is weak, so a game without a TD can be a low score. Weeks 3 and 4 were 9.8 and 6.4 points.

## Health and situation

Swift has no injury designation in your data. My searches did not turn up a 2026 week 9 report. The results were mostly 2025 stories (a groin injury and an absence that year), and I ignored them. I could not verify any current Swift injury or anything new this week.

The thing to watch is Kyle Monangai, who is Questionable with a toe injury. Your data shows he has a 23% opportunity share over his games this season. My searches did suggest a toe problem for him earlier in the 2026 season, but I could not confirm his status for Sunday. Toe injuries, turf toe especially, tend to linger. Players often return at reduced effectiveness and can re-aggravate it, so a first game back is usually a limited snap count. If Monangai returns and gets about a quarter of the work, Swift's 35% opportunity share could fall toward the low 30s. His share was 32% over the full season when Monangai was part of the picture. Johnson (14% share over the last 4) keeps the short-yardage touches that remain. Zavier Scott and Brittain Brown are on IR.

## Outlook

The projection is 136.4 points over the last 8 games (18.9 per game). That figure includes a schedule factor of 1.00, a usage trend of ×1.05 and a room factor of ×0.90 for Monangai's return. Week 10 is the bye.

- **Week 9** vs TB is a tough matchup.
- **Week 11** vs NO is an easy matchup.
- **Week 12** @ DET is tough.
- **Week 13** vs JAX is tough.

He is a weekly starter, and you should hold him. Floor games come in the 6–10 point range when he doesn't score. His ceiling is 25 points or more if he scores two TDs, as he did in Weeks 1, 6 and 8. I would not sell, because the goal-line role is what holds his value up and nothing in the numbers says it is going away. I would not pay a premium either, since the 3.8 yards per carry (3.2 over the last 4) and the Monangai return cap how far the average can rise. The best week is Week 11 against NO. Check Monangai's Sunday status before kickoff in Week 9.
